title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 5 — WORLD 6: B1+ TO B2 GATEWAY
description: An advanced bridge into B2 communication through precision vocabulary, complex grammar, natural listening, sustained speaking, structured writing, debate, presentation, and realistic problem-solving.
progression: B1+ fluency → B2 gateway → independent, flexible communication

targets.active_vocabulary: 1400+ words, collocations, phrasal verbs, word families and functional expressions
targets.reading: 1200–1400 words with inference, attitude, detail and main-idea questions
targets.listening: 10–12 minutes of natural-speed, multi-speaker English with accents and implied meaning
targets.conversation: 12–14 minutes of sustained interaction with follow-up questions, clarification and spontaneous responses
targets.writing: 300–350 words using clear structure, linking, examples, contrast and justification
targets.presentation: 6 minutes with introduction, organized points, examples, conclusion and audience questions
targets.real_life: travel, workplace, education, services, digital communication, complaints, negotiation, emergencies and social situations

missions.title: B2 Vocabulary Gateway — Precision & Collocation Power
missions.content: Build precise alternatives to common B1 words, learn strong verb-noun/adjective-noun combinations, identify formal and informal choices, and use new vocabulary in original sentences.

missions.title: Advanced Tense Control — Meaning, Not Memorization
missions.content: Choose tense forms according to sequence, duration, completion, background information, plans, predictions and current relevance.

missions.title: Past Modals — What Must Have Happened?
missions.content: Infer past situations, discuss missed opportunities, express certainty and uncertainty, and reconstruct events from evidence.

missions.title: Conditionals Lab — Hypotheses, Regrets & Alternatives
missions.content: Discuss unreal situations, past regrets, alternative outcomes and consequences while controlling conditional meaning and time reference.

missions.title: Relative Clauses & Information Density
missions.content: Combine short ideas into precise, natural sentences and use relative structures to describe people, places, systems and experiences.

missions.title: Passive & Reporting Structures — News and Information
missions.content: Transform information into formal and neutral structures used in news, reports, announcements, explanations and professional communication.

missions.title: Articles, Determiners & Reference Precision
missions.content: Improve accuracy when referring to known, general, specific, limited and contrasted information in connected communication.

missions.title: Connectors & Discourse — Sound Like a B2 Speaker
missions.content: Organize ideas with logical relationships, contrast, cause, consequence, addition, concession and examples instead of producing disconnected sentences.

missions.title: Register Mission — Casual, Neutral & Formal English
missions.content: Rewrite messages for friends, teachers, customers, managers and public services while preserving meaning and changing tone appropriately.

missions.title: B2 Conversation Lab — Twelve to Fourteen Minutes
missions.content: Sustain a long conversation about school, work, technology, travel and society; ask natural follow-up questions and keep interaction moving without translation.

missions.title: Reading Challenge — The Changing World
missions.content: Read an extended article about technology, education and social change, identify explicit and implied information, infer unfamiliar vocabulary from context and explain the writer's position.

missions.title: Listening Challenge — Real Voices, Real Speed
missions.content: Follow a 10–12 minute sequence of conversations, interviews and announcements; identify speaker purpose, attitude, key details and implied meaning.

missions.title: Writing Lab — Build a Strong Argument
missions.content: Write a structured opinion essay with a clear position, supporting reasons, examples, a contrasting idea and a logical conclusion using B2-level connectors.

missions.title: Presentation Lab — Explain, Compare & Defend
missions.content: Deliver an organized presentation on a real-world topic, transition between points, compare alternatives, explain evidence and respond to audience questions.

missions.title: Real-Life English — Travel, Booking & Unexpected Problems
missions.content: Handle delayed transport, booking mistakes, room problems, schedule changes and requests for compensation using clear, polite and flexible language.

missions.title: Real-Life English — Workplace & Education Mission
missions.content: Write and respond to practical workplace and school messages, discuss deadlines, request clarification, give constructive feedback and participate in a short meeting simulation.

missions.title: Debate Lab — Evidence, Counterarguments & Respectful Disagreement
missions.content: Develop a position, support it with reasons and examples, respond to opposing ideas and use respectful language such as I see your point, however... and It could be argued that...

missions.title: Complex Problem-Solving Simulation — One Day, Five Problems
missions.content: Solve a connected chain of realistic problems involving travel, money, technology, appointments and communication; explain choices and adapt when new information appears.

missions.title: B2 Gateway Integrated Skills Marathon
missions.content: Complete a demanding mixed-skills sequence: vocabulary in context, grammar editing, extended reading, natural listening, spontaneous speaking, structured writing and pronunciation repair.

missions.title: WORLD 6 MASTER QUEST — B1+ TO B2 GATEWAY
missions.content: Final mission combining advanced vocabulary, grammar transformation, inference reading, natural multi-speaker listening, sustained conversation, a six-minute presentation, a 300–350 word argument and a realistic problem-solving scenario.

quality_rules.difficulty: high for Grade 5, with a deliberate B2 gateway
quality_rules.assessment: production-first: learners must create language, not only recognize answers
quality_rules.progression: Each mission reuses and expands vocabulary and grammar from previous missions.
quality_rules.protected_note: This curriculum file adds Grade 5 World 6 only and does not modify Grade 2, Grade 3 or Grade 4.
